thread:
Laura: Heads up — since the eu-west egress-proxy rollout we see a ~5% spike in TLS failures. Packets show ALB returning the default cert instead of service cert. Anyone digging?
Ben: I saw traces too. TL;DR: envoy->egress-proxy is doing mTLS to upstream ALB, but SNI seems to be missing sometimes so ALB falls back to default.
Tanya: Is this correlated with HTTP/2 traffic? We recently enabled h2 on a few routes.
Ben: Yes, timed with the ALPN change. When client negotiates h2 and envoy upgrades, the upstream TLS handshake from egress-proxy occasionally doesn't include SNI (observed in tcpdump).
Sam: Can you paste the curl + tcpdump snippets?
Laura: Sure — here's a repro from a pod in eu-west: 
```
$ curl -v --http2 https://api.redwood-eu.internal/status
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* server certificate: CN=ELB-Default
* SSL: certificate subject: CN=ELB-Default
```
And tcpdump (filtered): 
```
12:34:56.789 IP pod->egress-proxy: ClientHello alpn: h2, sni: api.redwood-eu.internal
12:34:56.800 IP egress-proxy->alb: ClientHello alpn: h2, sni: <empty>
```
Ben: So egress-proxy is terminating TLS from pod, then doing mTLS to ALB but dropping SNI when ALPN is h2 in some handshakes. Could be a bug in our TLS stack or config (SNI proxying with mTLS + http2 interaction).
Tanya: ingress-bot can you show latest ingress annotations on the service?
ingress-bot: Current annotations on service/api-eu: ["alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/target-type":"ip", "alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol":"HTTPS", "external-traffic":"Local"]
Sam: Also noticed NAT egress IPs from the cluster changed yesterday (we rotated NAT64 for cost reasons). Might be a separate factor if ALB behavior is IP-based routing/target-group selection.
Ben: ALB shouldn't pick cert based on source IP, just SNI+listener rules. But default listener rule can match if SNI empty.
Tanya: Temporary mitigation idea: enable TLS passthrough for that route (preserve client SNI directly to ALB) until we root-cause. Can we flip that without breaking existing auth?
Laura: Passthrough would skip mTLS to ALB — we rely on client auth at the ALB for some flows, so need to ensure it still enforces mTLS.
Sam: Alternative: force egress-proxy to always forward SNI by copying :authority into SNI if missing — quick patch on envoy config?
Ben: I raised a small patch in the egress-proxy canary that sets server_name in upstream TLS context from the host header when missing. Rolling to 10% now. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy/e2: rollout started for egress-proxy-canary -> 10% at 2026-03-18T10:12:00Z
Laura: Good — monitoring: increase SNI-missing metric alerts and chest dump TLS handshakes for 1h.
Tanya: Also add ALPN logging on ALB side (if possible) and check for HTTP/2->http1.1 downgrade counts.
Sam: Noted. If canary looks good, we'll roll to 100% and then re-evaluate whether we need an ALB listener default-cert swap (avoid serving default cert to prod hostnames).
Ben: Filing a follow-up ticket with traces + tcpdumps and the envoy patch link.
Laura: Thanks team — keeping this thread for post-mortem. If anyone sees a spike in client 526/525 TLS errors, ping here. :rotating_light:
